body.justification: The theorem gives matching lower and feasible-estimator upper bounds over the same full-design-centered class.
body.gap: The corrected frontier replaces the false iid-spacing upper rate by the sharp log-adjusted geometric-mixing rate.
body.consumer: Designers can identify which of replication, calendar coverage, or donor precision is rate limiting.
body.proof_tex:
For a channel \(q\), let \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) be the pair supplied by \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, let its two target values be \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  The pair has affinity at least \(a_0>0\) and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\), where the spacing component of \(R_q\) is \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).  For every estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E_0'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E_1'=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Consequently
\[
P_{0,q}(E_0')+P_{1,q}(E_1')
\ge\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\ge a_0,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge \frac{a_0\Delta_q^2}{8}
\ge cR_q.
\tag{12}
\]
Taking the maximum over the four channels, then the supremum over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and finally the infimum over estimators proves the lower bound \(cR_{\star,\beta}\).

For the upper bound, condition on \(\mathscr X\), \(E_0\), and the donor sample.  By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, the estimation error on a successful fit is the sum of four terms:
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{13}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}
=\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{hist}}
=\sum_{s,i}\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\(B_{\mathrm{LP}}\) is the Taylor remainder, and \(B_{\mathrm{don}}\) is the difference between the weighted regression surface at the fold centers and at \(z_0\).

The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums conditional on the displayed conditioning sigma-field.  Conditional cross-unit independence and boundedness therefore give
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\tag{14}
\]
and, using \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control},
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{15}
\]
No temporal independence inside a unit history is used in (15).

On the kernel support, \(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2\le C_Kh_{sk}\).  The deterministic weight bound and the Taylor remainder therefore yield
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|
\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_k h_{sk}^{\lambda}.
\tag{16}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\), use fixed \(S,K_D\), and apply Cauchy--Schwarz to (16).  On the good sample,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mid E_0]
\le C\left\{
R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}
\right\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{17}
\]
because \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}=R_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For a donor complement of size \(m_k\), independence and the fourth-moment calculation used in the honest-interval proof give
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\left\{m_k^{-1}\sum_{j\notin k}Z_j-z_0\right\}
\right\|_2^4\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
\le Cm_k^{-2}.
\tag{18}
\]
Projection onto the cube and donor ellipticity change the right side only by a fixed constant.  On the event where the resulting norm is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local modulus bounds the squared fold discrepancy by a constant times that norm to power \(2\kappa\).  Lyapunov's inequality applied to (18) yields \(Cm_k^{-\kappa}\).  On its complement, boundedness of the surfaces and Markov's inequality applied to (18) give \(Cm_k^{-2}\).  Since the number of folds is fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{19}
\]

The raw fitted intercept is bounded on every successful fit by \(B\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2}\), while a failed intercept is defined as zero.  Thus the squared estimation error is uniformly bounded by a fixed constant on the bad sample.  The bad-sample probability bound in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes its risk contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  Combining (13)--(19) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{20}
\]

For completeness, the smoothing term is never uniquely active.  With
\(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\), weighted arithmetic--geometric mean gives, cohort by cohort,
\[
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}
\le an_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
After weighting and summing,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}+T^{-2\lambda/d}
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}.
\tag{21}
\]
Equations (12) and (20) establish the asserted same-class bracket in every relative-growth regime.  The covariance estimator is feasible by spectral clipping, but neither (18) nor the estimator requires the donor law to be homoskedastic or Gaussian.
